newsitem.title: MONACO: RALLYING-MCRAE PULLS OUT AS MAKINEN TAKES LEAD.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-MCRAE PULLS OUT AS MAKINEN TAKES LEAD.

text.p: Briton Colin McRae retired from the Monte Carlo rally after Tuesday's, icy first test in the Vercors mountains which allowed Finn Tommi Makinen to seize the race lead.

McRae, who had dropped to fourth place overall after hitting a snowdrift on Monday, went off the road again in the third day's opening timed stage over 33 kms from St Jean en Royans to La Chapelle en Vercors.

The 1995 world champion broke the rear left suspension and damaged the steering of his new Subaru Impreza, his team said. He managed to finish the stage despite a badly damaged rear left wheel but ended it over 24 minutes behind his Subaru team mate Piero Liatti of Italy, who clocked the best time.
As no technical assistance was allowed before the start of the next section, McRae had to pull out, his team added.
The second fastest time 13 seconds slower than Liatti was enough to give reigning world champion Makinen first place in the overall placings in his Mitsubishi Lancer.
Overnight leader Carlos Sainz of Spain, who had started the day three seconds ahead of Makinen, could only manage the third fastest time and lost 18 seconds on his rival.
With five timed stages remaining on the penultimate day of the winter classic, Makinen was in the lead with Liatti in second place eight seconds behind and Sainz third a further seven seconds back.
